title: Epochal checkpointed eviction to preserve prefix causal consistency under continuous batching
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Continuous batching and aggressive GPU memory reclamation can cause KV cache entries associated with in-flight prefix contexts to be evicted during overlapping requests. This leads to silent correctness issues: regenerated KV entries diverge (different lengths/tokens) or cause model state rollbacks when batches replay or when model variants are used as fallbacks. Goal: define and implement a deterministic eviction protocol that guarantees prefix-causal correctness while enabling compact GPU memory usage and predictable performance for high-throughput workloads.

Summary of proposed approach: introduce 'epochal checkpoints' per request prefix cohort. Each checkpoint binds a small monotonic epoch ID and a lightweight 'live set' fingerprint for the prefix (not full tokens). Eviction decisions must respect two invariants: 1) epoch monotonicity: entries created under epoch E cannot be reclaimed until no active request references epoch E or a newer checkpoint supersedes it, and 2) prefix-affinity safety: if a reclaimed entry would be re-materialized for an in-flight prefix within threshold latency, we must either pin it or perform a transparent synchronous fetch to avoid divergence. The runtime will use a hybrid LRU+TTL policy where epoch pins temporarily raise item priority and a background compactor performs epoch-aligned slab reclamation to defragment GPU memory.

Why this is different: instead of heuristic prefix pinning or global conservative TTLs, epochal checkpoints provide a fine-grained, low-footprint safety mechanism that composes with continuous batching and multi-model fallbacks. This reduces unnecessary pins, improves reclamation, and gives an auditable correctness boundary for rollouts and debugging.
acceptance_criteria: Design doc reviewed and approved by Runtime and Inference teams
Unit and integration tests cover: epoch pin/unpin semantics, concurrent eviction during batching, and fallback re-materialization correctness
Benchmark: end-to-end tail latency increase <= 5% for production prefix distribution versus baseline when running with epochal checkpoints enabled
GPU memory reclaimed rates show >=12% improvement over conservative TTL-only baseline on standard Llama-like workload
Canary rollout in dedicated pool with automatic rollback on divergence alerts
Observability: per-prefix epoch metric, eviction-audit logs, and a debugging endpoint that maps evicted keys to epoch history
notes: Alternative considered: strict prefix lease (long pins) — simpler but causes memory pressure and poor GPU utilization for multi-tenant workloads
Alternative considered: probabilistic LRU with heuristics based on access histograms — lower guarantee surface and harder to reason about correctness under batching
Trade-offs: epochal checkpoints add small metadata (8-16 bytes per active prefix) and requires a fast atomic counter; complexity grows with number of concurrent prefix cohorts
Security: epoch metadata is not customer data; still ensure it is cleared on private deployments per retention policy
Interaction with quantization: eviction and re-materialization must respect quantized kernels; we will validate re-materialized tensors across f16/int8 kernels for bit-compatibility where required
implementation_steps: 1. Add epoch counter and checkpoint data structure in KV manager (C++ runtime)
2. Integrate epoch pins into the continuous batching scheduler to mark active prefix cohorts
3. Implement hybrid eviction policy: base LRU + TTL + epoch pin boost
4. Implement background epoch-aligned compactor for slab reclamation
5. Expose metrics and audit logs (prometheus counters + structured log lines)
6. Add tests (unit/integration/e2e) and a deterministic eviction emulator for fuzzing
7. Perf run + canary rollout + post-mortem and adjustments
comments: 2026-01-16 - Aisha Patel: Initial design spike completed. PoC shows epoch pins reduce false-positive evictions during 2x sustained batching. Link: https://drive.redwood.ai/designs/epochal-eviction-spike
2026-01-22 - Ethan Morales: Implemented epoch counter and pin/unpin APIs. Observed a 10% memory overhead in worst-case path; will optimize metadata layout.
2026-01-30 - Review (Runtime): Review feedback: ensure compactor avoids creating long pauses on GPU; prefer incremental slab moves. Action: add incremental compaction phase.

2026-02-02 - QA: Added deterministic eviction emulator harness. Found race where batched replay could reference an epoch that was unpinned earlier than expected. Root cause: batching scheduler cleaned prefix marks prior to request finalization. Fix: move unpin to request finalize hook.
